newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products - mogas looking to ship out.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products - mogas looking to ship out.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mixed on Monday, traders said.
Gas oil traders tried to shift material out of the region in a market hit by weaker futures.

"We have had quite a bit of interest from people looking to move product west and east," said one who thought the arb worked marginally better westwards. Good supplies in recent weeks have pressured prices in the Med to the point where arbs have opened.
Heating oil was talked around flat fob quotes to +$1 for mid month delivery while Russian was offered around cif high quotes - 50 cents.
Two Libyan cargoes traded on Friday at high fob quotes +$1.50.
Straight-run fuel oil prices held steady despite weaker crude and crack fuel oil. Traders said the market was supported in South and North on perceptions of refinery crude run-cuts.

They said there were good supplies of straight run material in both regions, but while crude refining margins remain poor they expected demand for straight-run barrels as a feed stock to stay healthy.
The buying interest saw Suez barrels valued around $103 a tonne cif Med with Russian M40 fuel oil $10 higher.

Low octane gasoline saw some support and was assessed around $10-$11 dollars a tonne below eurograde. Higher octane gasoline lost ground with little demand seen and talked around $205 on an fob Med basis.
Traders said that although the market was currently quite choppy it would have balanced out by March, supported by refinery run cuts said to have already started in Italy.
Naphtha markets were quiet with levels softer in line with the losses seen on IPE gas oil.
